metadata.baseline: First ready-state prefetch: one system attempt per batch, per-task admission updates
metadata.summaryMethod: Median of three per-run values; latency columns are medians of per-run percentiles, not pooled percentiles. Ratios compare medians. Ranges preserve run variation.
accounting: CPUSeconds measures PostgreSQL container CPU while Workers run, including system admission, claims, finalization and observer work.
TotalSQLMs and TotalSharedHits sum top-level pg_stat_statements, avoiding double-counting nested PL/pgSQL statements. SQL time is elapsed query time, not CPU time.

EnqueueSeconds and EnqueueCPUSeconds cover blocked-rule setup (blocked scenarios) and all blocked/runnable inserts, including grouping triggers. They exclude serial-history setup, schema migration, Worker construction and VACUUM ANALYZE. Docker CPU-read round trips add fixed wall-clock overhead.
elapsedPlusEnqueueSeconds and cpuPlusEnqueueSeconds are medians of each run's enqueue+execution sum; they are not full migration-to-drain timings.

Claim transaction timings include transaction overhead. PrefetchReadyTasks is reported separately; FinalizeTaskAttempt includes the baseline per-round system deferrals; the after version keeps one scheduler attempt.
Context cancellation at shutdown is excluded from SQLSTATE acceptance. JSON logs are retained separately; rollback connection-close errors are reported rather than hidden.
PrefetchReadyTasks operation Rows counts returned SQL result rows, not the number of prepared tasks; throughput always counts completed business tasks.
PoolWaitSeconds is the delta of pgx cumulative AcquireDuration, including immediate acquisitions; it is not a pure wait-time histogram. PoolWaits is EmptyAcquireCount.
limitations: Finite, warmed synthetic workloads on one host; three repeats do not provide confidence intervals or production capacity.
Blocked cases use one full tag group, quota zero and higher task weight; high group cardinality and heterogeneous label routing are not covered by timed benchmarks.
No chaos or other stress suites run concurrently with timed benchmarks; an unrelated existing background container remains.
Ready reservations add a state write and can occupy finite quota before a Worker starts execution.
This compares the two requested optimizations together, including the extra control slot and skipped redundant cursor writes. It is not an ablation of the long loop versus bulk UPDATE.
metadata.change: Long-lived prefetch under one lease; bulk fresh unconstrained admission; two control slots; avoid unchanged cursor writes. No event-driven wakeup.
